articles.name: Litmus
articles.long_description:
At Litmus, we’re building evals for humans and redefining how talent is evaluated. Teams like Mercor, Wispr, Composio, Neo Scholars, Astranis, and more are already using Litmus to build their technical teams.

Every company in the world will soon be powered by neo-humans (agent assisted people). But building evals to measure neo-human performance is unexplored and difficult. It requires systematically benchmarking neo-human capabilities and failure modes across all sectors of knowledge work, developing reproducible environments that test neo-human performance on complex tasks, and designing causal attribution frameworks over execution trajectories to identify and validate reproducible action sequences and decision patterns that lead to successful outcomes.

At Litmus, we’re solving this problem. We deliver hiring insights to companies by capturing how candidates use tools, reason, and make decisions in their interviews, giving agentic graders the evidence to evaluate candidate skillset and predict job performance.

articles.name: Rise Reforming
articles.long_description:
Geopolitical conflicts and natural disasters frequently expose the vulnerability of the American chemical industry. The reason? Production is centralized and fossil fuel-dependent. The solution? Localized production using an undervalued resource: biogas. The US produces enough biogas to make over $20 bn/y worth of chemicals, but 60% is wasted in low-margin applications or flared altogether.

Rise Reforming is commercializing a modular process to transform this underutilized biogas on-site into cheap, supply-secure chemicals. Our beachhead market is dimethyl ether (DME), used as an aerosol propellant and a low-carbon fuel additive in propane. Our target market is methanol: an established billion $ chemical and the future of low-carbon shipping.

We're doing our pilot project at a Chicagoland wastewater plant. This will be the first wastewater biogas-to-methanol demo in the Americas.

We're hiring for a senior chemical process engineer. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/rise-reforming/jobs/wJ9Q9nv-senior-chemical-process-engineer

articles.name: HyperProbe
articles.long_description:
With tools like Cursor and Claude Code, writing software is no longer the bottleneck. Debugging is. Agents cannot fix production crashes using logs and traces that were sized for human eyeballs. The gap is missing data.

HyperProbe allows agents to debug live software autonomously. Our SDK drops non-breaking probes straight into running services to read exact variable states from memory at the moment of failure, instead of reasoning backwards from flat logs.

Zero redeploys. Under 1% CPU overhead. Automatic PII redaction.

We turn 4-hour production war rooms into 10-minute automated resolutions. As agents write and operate more of the world's software, HyperProbe is the runtime observability layer that lets them understand what they built.
articles.one_liner: AI engineer that debugs and fixes production incidents in realtime

articles.name: Floracene
articles.long_description:
Floracene lets any healthcare operator describe the internal tool they need and deploy it in one click - connected to production data, with read and write access scoped by the user. Think Lovable or Retool, except purpose-built for the needs of healthcare business that has no engineering team.

The bottleneck in healthcare isn't building anymore. Anyone can vibecode an 80% solution in an afternoon, custom to their own workflow, with people already on staff. The tool then dies locally on the builder’s computer, because IT (correctly) won't let anyone deploy a tool touching PHI without first-class authentication and permissioning. Our first customer had multiple employees who had each built useful tools and dashboards locally, but couldn’t actually share these with coworkers or connect to their core practice data. Within weeks of implementing Floracene, they were able to consolidate their BI tooling into Floracene and shipped 4 net-new to production.

A staggering ~$200B is spent on administrative software in healthcare every year in the US. Tens of thousands of those companies still run core operations on spreadsheets, and we're at the top of the first inning of AI adoption.

Asaph and Jonah met on the hospitals team at Palantir two years ago, and have each spent the last four years in the plumbing of US healthcare: claims, eligibility, and payor contracting. Asaph was an early PM at Garner. Jonah was a founding engineer at Metriport (YC S22) after starting his own fax-automation startup for fertility clinics.

articles.name: Rindler
articles.long_description:
We build Maxxwell, a desktop app for people who run several coding agents at once.

Past two or three sessions, you become the bottleneck. Every session asks you something, most of it small, and you spend the day answering instead of deciding. It is also hard to tell which sessions are making progress, which are stuck on something trivial, and which have quietly started building the wrong thing.

Maxxwell puts every session in one window and marks each one working, idle, or waiting on you. On top of that sits an orchestrator, a real coding-agent session of its own that reads the others and reports back. You talk to it instead of to twelve terminals. It tells you what landed, what it decided for you, and what actually needs your call.

Every worker is your own tool, unmodified. Claude Code, Codex and Cursor Agent run in real terminal sessions you can attach to and take over at any point

articles.name: Robocurve
articles.long_description:
Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust.

Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits.

Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once.

Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the field of robotics evals barely exists. Whoever builds the trusted measure of robot capability becomes the reference everyone relies on. We combine backgrounds in AI evals and robotics to build and grow this field as fast as possible. We already shipped v1 of our open-source framework, Inspect Robots, and ran our first pilot scoring a frontier model on a real robot.
articles.one_liner: Evals for robots

articles.name: Glen
articles.long_description:
Glen is the layer that unifies every agent your company runs. Glen pulls in agent sessions from Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, plus Slack messages, GitHub prs, tickets, docs and calls. When a new agent picks up a task, Glen finds relevant prior context and injects it in the agents context window to steer it, producing knowledge work that is significantly higher quality, faster and cheaper.

Glen does more. You can query the original agent behind any line of code, or search every session your org has ever run. It distills what your team does into skills and surfaces the right one automatically. Agents work multiplayer, picking up the style and context of whoever else is on the file. Transcripts are unified across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, so you can hand a session from one to another mid-task. And Glen can also double as a company brain, from Slack, in app, or by just installing Glen on any agent.

We’re building toward a future where memory is no longer the missing piece of intelligence. A future where every agent maintains a lossless and continuous thread of institutional experience enabling the era of the compounding organization and fully unsupervised digital labour.

articles.name: Datoric
articles.long_description:
Datoric develops custom datasets for robotics, treating research, collection, verification, and production as one continuous process. We work closely with frontier model teams to turn emerging limitations and model failures into testable data hypotheses, and run exclusive collections for specific data methods based on results.

Data is collected through private invite-only applications separated by modality, customer, and trust level. Every submission remains linked to the contributor, device, task, session, consent, rights, and processing history that produced it, giving our internal QA and fraud models the context to detect problems that may appear legitimate in the finished file. 

Once a collection method is validated, we scale it up as a solution to the model failure and it also becomes a reusable data recipe for future custom projects or independently collected, rights-cleared data products.

articles.name: Induction Labs
articles.long_description:
We are scaling foundation models that are curious about the world.

We’ve seen general intelligence appear exactly once, and its hallmark has been curiosity: a dissatisfaction with what we already know about the world, an ability to learn from world experience, and a disposition to share knowledge with other individuals. Across generations, these human traits have built modern science, technology, and culture.

We think superintelligence will come from models that work the same way: learning from their own observation, updating as they go, growing what they know. These models will start from what humanity knows and discover past us.

We believe that scaling curious intelligence is a defining problem of our time. If solved, we will live to see a new era of technological advances, scientific understanding, and human flourishing.

articles.name: OS3
articles.long_description:
OS3 is building the platform that makes intelligent robots accessible to every business.

Today, robotics is constrained by two fundamental bottlenecks: hardware is too expensive to deploy at scale, and robots are difficult to train because high-quality robotics data is scarce and costly to collect. 

We built OS3 to solve both.

Our two-person team designed and a US-made mobile humanoid robot for a fraction of the cost of commercial alternatives. On the intelligence side, instead of relying on expensive robot-generated training data, we trained our own video-action model on 150,000 hours of real-world video spanning more than 2,000 tasks. Every deployed robot feeds new experience into our reinforcement learning pipeline, self improving robot fleet over time.

This creates a robot that can be deployed across industries to automate repetitive, physical work without requiring a new robot or training pipeline for every task. Our robots are already deployed in hotels, with customers now expanding the platform into biotech, hospitals, and data centers, including a wet lab at Stanford.

Our mission is to do for robotics what Apple did for personal computing: take technology that was once expensive, specialized, and inaccessible and make it powerful and usable at massive scale. We’re building toward a world with billions of intelligent robots, and OS3 is the platform that makes that possible.

articles.name: Dualizer
articles.long_description:
Dualizer builds AI-powered, physics-based process simulation and digital twins to design and scale chemical processes and optimize existing plants. We help engineering teams identify bottlenecks, increase yield and throughput, and reduce energy and production costs—improving plant efficiency and profitability.

The platform combines AI reasoning, our proprietary deterministic simulation and optimization engine, and physics-informed machine learning. Engineers can build, calibrate, and refine models through conversation, starting from a diagram, available data, or an engineering objective. Calculations account for thermodynamics, material and energy balances, equipment behavior, and operating constraints, enabling teams to optimize interconnected equipment and operating conditions across a plant.

Equipment sizing and costing, 3D layout planning, and techno-economic analysis connect process improvements to plant-level decisions. Teams can accelerate new process scale-up, debottleneck operating plants, and continually refine operating strategies as production targets and plant conditions change. Dualizer makes rigorous simulation and optimization an ongoing capability for improving industrial productivity and profitability throughout a plant’s life.

articles.name: Reific
articles.long_description:
Reific builds RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time, for the frontier labs that train agents. AI has learned to reason over text and code. But most of what matters in the real world shows up as numbers that change every second: a heartbeat, a gearbox, a GPU cluster. No human can track thousands of signals at once, but AI should be able to.

In our environments, data streams in on a clock while the agent works, and every action is graded by what actually happened. Most AI training today teaches models to match human experts. We treat human performance as the floor. Each environment comes from real, de-identified records, in three task families: personal agents, industry, and science & compute.

Today, even the best frontier model averages under 50% on each family. Training an open model on our environments raised its full-solve rate on unseen tasks by 54% (from 25.6% to 39.5%), with no loss on general benchmarks. Our mission is to build the infrastructure that keeps AI climbing the frontier, long past human level in the real world.

articles.name: Plover Labs
articles.long_description:
Plover Labs is building toward a future where AI agents write, ship, and maintain most of a company's software. We make it possible for agents to own real engineering roles, not just suggest code for someone else to approve.

Coding models keep getting more capable, but enterprise adoption lags behind AI-native startups because enterprises don't yet trust agent output. Each codebase has conventions, history, and failure modes that a general-purpose model doesn't know. We learn those continuously from the code, how the team works, and the mistakes agents make. Then we fix the codebase and add merge gates that use deterministic verifiers instead of another model's judgment, so the same mistake can't ship twice. As the gates build up, agents can be trusted with more of the work.

We have five-figure monthly contracts with Series C companies Envoy and Fieldguide. At Fieldguide, we tripled PRs per engineer in one quarter, with the same headcount and PR size.

articles.name: Organizely
articles.long_description:
Organizely helps American manufacturers use AI to lower production costs. 

Factories depend on three resources: materials, equipment, and labor. Costs rise unexpectedly when components are missing, machines go down, or staffing doesn’t match demand. We experienced this firsthand while owning and operating a factory in the U.S. for six years. As we scaled, it was expensive to resolve factory-wide bottlenecks quickly and it became harder to stay competitive on price. 

Other companies are trying to layer AI agents on top of legacy ERPs to do logistics work, but the underlying data architectures limit how much those agents can understand and do. So we’re building a new ERP from the ground up for the era of AI. 

Organizely is an AI-native ERP with AI reasoning and machine learning algorithms embedded throughout for a single intelligent platform that can model, predict, and act. We natively automate all core manufacturing workflows including demand planning, raw material tracking, machine maintenance, and production scheduling. 

Organizely continuously improves over time, suggesting new ways for manufacturers to reduce costs and produce more with their existing facilities and teams. It's the whole factory solved. 

We’ve deployed to factories across six U.S. states and now we’re bringing AI to all factories across America. 🇺🇸

articles.long_description: At least 94% of US outage minutes start on the distribution grid, and most utilities are blind between the substation and the meter. Evardi builds a live model of a utility’s network from data it already has, matching every meter to its transformer and using virtual meters to show load and solar on every transformer. On top of that model, our AI agents do the engineering work utilities need at the grid edge: checking switching orders, finding outages after extreme weather and planning for new load from DERs and data centers. We’re working with utilities across the globe that together serve over 10 million customers.

articles.name: Ailit
articles.long_description:
Ailit is building the electric energy system for North American freight rail. Our first product, Superwagon, is a battery wagon designed to power existing diesel-electric locomotives, allowing railroads to electrify the fleets they already own.

Superwagon carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive’s existing electric motors. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones along the route and recharged off-board, providing operators with limitless range.

We deliver energy as a service, owning and operating the batteries and swapping sites. Railroads pay for energy with no upfront equipment purchase, with pricing set at 20% below today’s diesel cost.

Founded in Stockholm by Christian Lind and Emil Tagesson, our team is now based in San Francisco. We’re building our first full-scale prototype, and it’s being prepared to move a locomotive on battery power in the coming days.

articles.name: Taan.ai
articles.long_description:
Taan builds foundation music models that do what you tell them to, when you tell them to. We're starting with music for video. Give Taan a video and it watches it, then composes an original score that follows the emotion and timing of every cut. If the scene is tense for 10 seconds and then turns happy, the music changes at that exact moment. You get back a fully mixed .mp4. Agents and apps call Taan through our API, so any video tool can add scored, synced music with one call. 

Today's music models can make catchy tracks, but you can't steer them. Ask for "violin at exactly the 11th second" and they usually skip it. We trained Taan from the ground up for control.

We work with teams building video agents, ad and creative tools, micro-dramas and games. We're musicians and ML researchers. articles.name: Superserve
articles.long_description:
Superserve gives every AI agent its own computer in the cloud. Each one is an isolated VM that starts in under 50ms, sleeps between turns, and picks up exactly where it left off, for hours, weeks or indefinitely.

Traditional cloud infrastructure was built to run one app for many users. Agents flip that. Each agent needs its own isolated machine where it can write and run code, use tools and work on its own for long stretches. Everything it produces has to persist the whole time, the way your laptop keeps your work.

That means agent computers have to be stateful, secure and cheap to run. For agents that talk to customers, they also have to start, sleep and wake almost instantly.

Fast - Machines start in under 50ms, either cold or from a template with your repo and dependencies already loaded. You don't need to keep a pool of servers running and waiting.

Persistent - Paused machines keep their full memory and disk state at zero compute cost. They can resume or fork from that exact state. Pausing and resuming is fast enough that a machine can sleep between inference calls and wake on the next turn. Agents can run Docker, databases, browsers or any other service inside.

Secure - Every machine is a microVM with its own kernel. You can program the rules for what traffic can come in and go out, and they're enforced at the network boundary where the agent can't reach them. API secrets are handled at the network layer too, so they never enter the machine. Every action is logged for audits.

Teams building coding agents, autonomous workers, and eval or RL training environments use Superserve to give every agent session or rollout its own machine, with no infrastructure to manage.

We run 100K+ machines every week for teams including Lindy and Y Combinator.
articles.one_liner: Virtual machines for long-running agents

Synara is the AI monitoring station for the cameras that are already installed. It needs no new hardware and watches day and night. It understands far more than intruders: falls, guns, fights. Synara verifies incidents in seconds, talks intruders down on site or sends police a verified alarm, then coordinates with officers on who’s on site and where people are safe, until the insurance claim is resolved.

Because AI does the watching, monitoring becomes drastically cheaper and more accurate. Synara sells through security integrators under their own brand, so every camera they’ve installed becomes recurring revenue.

articles.name: Super Powers Mobility (SPM)
articles.long_description:
We started off building the highest performance, 470 volt electric off-road vehicles but we realized our ultra power dense battery packs are useful for mobile and stationary energy storage and power export, for military and consumer use cases. We develop battery packs, power electronics, and traction powertrain systems for vehicles.

For the majority of 2026 we were marketing our electric off-road vehicles, but we pivoted to selling our high performance battery packs and power export capabilities in the month of September. We went from having $769,000 in consumer pre-orders (possibly low conversion rate to sales) to $421,815 in realized revenue in 1 month, with a $792,000 qualified pipeline. 

Our tech is so compelling because the safety and layout of high voltage battery packs has only been mastered by large, well funded OEM companies who have brought it in-house. That means all other companies without the in-house expertise rely on battery companies to develop packs, and power electronics companies to develop power export capabilities. SPM has both of those capabilities in-house so we can ensure a fast turnaround and much more reliable product. 

One of the biggest priorities of the department of war is energy dominance. We're seeing it constantly in new solicitations. Our strategy is superior - become a prime, but simultaneously service primes because most of then don't actually have the battery and power electronics expertise we have.

Founded by Jon Powers - Ex-Tesla Sr. Mechanical Integration Engineer leading Cybertruck vehicle integration.

articles.name: Armorer Labs
articles.long_description:
Armorer helps companies in regulated industries ship their own AI systems faster and keep them secure in production.

Most security tools flag an issue and file a ticket. Armorer assesses your agent and simulates attacks to find the real issues. Then it creates a verified fix that stops the attack without breaking the business, ready for your approval in about 4 hours.

In production, Armorer checks every agent action in milliseconds, with no GPU needed. It detects malicious behavior such as prompt injection, goal hijacking and data leaks, then allows, holds or denies the action.

Armorer's detection models beat every other detector we tested on six public benchmarks. Armorer is 22% more accurate than JEV while being 88x faster, so users won't feel the delay.

We spent years building and evaluating AI security systems together at AWS, including its first customer-facing AI security agent, which scaled to 100k+ customers. Armorer is backed by Paul Vixie, an internet pioneer inducted into the Internet Hall of Fame in 2014.

Self-sovereign payment processing. Send an invoice straight from the wallet. Get paid from your web checkout. No middleman.
Easy fiat on/off ramps. Move stablecoins to USD and back without the pain.
Built for agentic commerce. Manage per-agent sub-wallets for agentic workflows.

Most wallets and payment processors don’t work FOR you. They're slow, route your payments in the way that earns them the most, and they leak your financial life to anyone asking. Worse: every single one hold the keys to your money.

Multi-chain, non-custodial, end-to-end encrypted wallet. 
Your keys, your money, your assets: you are in full control of your funds at all times. 
Least Cost Routing. Every swap and payment takes the cheapest path, not the one that pays a middleman the most.
Self-sovereign payment processing. Send an invoice straight from the wallet. Get paid from your web checkout. No middleman.
Easy fiat on/off ramps. Move stablecoins to USD and back without the pain.
Built for agentic commerce. Manage per-agent sub-wallets for agentic workflows.
Encrypted by default. Protecting you from bad actors and surveillance capitalism.

🔥Early traction

Signed our first major LOI with @Trustboop (founded by Justice Laub of Drone Racing League and Rob Rhinehart of Soylent).

Onboarding our first enterprise customer in ecommerce packaging and marketing, doing about $1.5M/month in volume. They've connected us to 10 more companies in the same vertical at similar volume, roughly a $100M/yr GMV opportunity.

Josh and Manuel led the creation of MobileCoin, the cryptocurrency in Signal Messenger: $100M+ raised, $1.16B peak valuation, $4B+ peak coin market cap, acquired in 2026. They understand what it takes to build a cryptographic business.

Michael runs product and design. He's an internationally exhibited artist with two published art books, and he builds beautiful products.

Manuel runs operations and orchestrates systems that actually work at scale.

Intros to businesses moving $1M+/month in payments, especially cross-border, ecommerce, and DTC, who want lower fees and more control over their funds.

Strategic partners in fintech and payments interested in integrating our infrastructure.

articles.name: Tilo
articles.long_description:
Tilo gives AI agents one shared computer. Today every agent gets its own virtual machine and works by screenshots and clicks, which is slow, expensive and brittle. Agents that work together have to describe what they did to each other in messages.

Tilo is a Linux-based operating system built for agents as users. Every app exports typed actions that agents call over MCP while people use the same actions as buttons, on the same live state. Many agents work in one workspace at once and read each other's work instead of messaging about it. Every change is attributed and can be undone, and irreversible actions need permission. Because state and interface are separate, agents can generate an app's entire UI on demand.

On the same multi-app task with the same model, agents on Tilo were about 29× cheaper and 90× faster than computer use, which failed. A small model on Tilo did it for about 1/10,000 of the frontier model's cost. In our scale test, 50 agents worked in one shared workspace on a single laptop, at about 60 MB of memory per agent. Tilo runs headless, in our cloud, or as a desktop, and you can open any workspace from the browser.
articles.one_liner: The Microsoft of the AI era: the operating system for AI agents.

articles.name: Altair Health
articles.long_description:
Altair is an AI-native medical billing service for independent practices. We take over a practice's billing end to end and get doctors paid by insurers. AI does the work; our billers handle the exceptions.

That can only work if a practice can trust an agent alone with its revenue. So we formalized insurers' billing policies and put a theorem prover under the agent. Before the agent acts on a claim, the prover checks the action against that insurer's policies, and anything that fails goes to one of our billers. 

Every claim teaches Altair how each insurer behaves, so the longer we run a practice's billing, the better we predict what its insurers will pay, deny or delay.

We're building the default way a new practice gets paid: a doctor connects their EHR and bills clean, completely self-serve and on auto-pilot.

Altair will be the financial platform every independent practice in America starts on and stays on. And to the Health Insurers' "Delay, Deny, Defend", we say "Predict, Prevent, Prevail".

articles.name: Graphide
articles.long_description:
Graphide CI runs your CI 10-20× faster than GitHub runners on enterprise deployments, and our 24/7 agents optimize the CI itself, not just the machines. For teams with big CI bills that haven't been optimized, we cut costs 70%+ and take over the ongoing work of optimizing CI, so you can focus on your product.

We're faster and cheaper because we own both the hardware and the optimizations and configs that run on it, which lets us do what owning only one could not. A graph of the codebase runs only the tests each change can reach, and we run your tests in parallel, so your CI is limited only by the length of your longest test. Our agents then tune machines, caches and test splits as you add more tests and code over time. We also patch the tests themselves, fixing flakes and adding our own libraries so they run faster and more reliably.

Coding agents now write more code than teams can check, making verification the new bottleneck. CI is where we start, but we also cover the rest of the verification stack. Our PR review agent runs the old and new code in live environments, finding bugs and proving them by writing tests (50% more bugs found than Greptile on our benchmarks, with 35% fewer false positives). Our visualizer shows data flows and graph-based diffs so you can understand a PR in seconds.
articles.one_liner: 10-20× faster CI runners + 24/7 agent cutting bloated CI bills 70+%

articles.name: Sutrix
articles.long_description:
Sutrix turns messy data from EHRs, clinical notes, wearables, and surveys into clean, study-ready datasets allowing healthcare research teams to deliver tailored patient care faster.

Before a clinical study can start, research staff spend weeks pulling patient data from disconnected systems like the EHR, REDCap, and wearable platforms, reading notes chart by chart, and reconciling conflicting entries in spreadsheets. Sutrix automates that work by deploying AI systems within each team’s own environment, linking patient records across sources, applying the study's rules, and flagging unclear cases for staff to review.

Paying research teams at 10+ institutions cut data prep by 80% going from months per study to weeks.

We're brothers who've built together for 4 years. We first solved this problem doing forward-deployed work at HSS, where we built an injury surveillance system now used by 700+ teams. Ritvik's clinical research at HSS and Emory showed us every research team has the same bottleneck. Supratik previously founded and exited an ai security company backed by a16z Speedrun, and built production AI agents at Amazon.

articles.name: ChemPilot.ai
articles.long_description:
ChemPilot accelerates the discovery and development of next generation defense materials using AI and data from our automated wet lab. Developing a new material today takes 10+ years of trial and error. We compress that to months by screening for what can actually be made, then closing the loop: every lab result feeds back into the models so the next round is faster and smarter.

Sam, Ofir and Maor spent two years researching these materials at the Technion lab of our CSO, Prof. Alon Grinberg Dana (former MIT postdoc), working directly with defense primes and government R&D agencies. Together we bring chemical engineering, computational chemistry and AI, plus the production systems to put them to work. ChemPilot spun out of that research.

The West’s defense and dual-use industrial base runs on materials with fragile, sole-source and often adversarial supply chains. Demand for new capability is surging, and materials still take decades to develop. We’re building a new kind of chemical prime: one that can discover, develop and ultimately manufacture the materials the West needs, securely, fast and at cost.

articles.name: Rodeo Robotics
articles.long_description:
Rodeo Robotics (YC F26) automates vehicle maintenance so shops can get vehicles back to work at lower cost.

Co-founders Michael Hazard and Colby Duke met at Applied Intuition, where they helped OEMs like Toyota and General Motors deploy autonomy in the real world and saw firsthand how much hands-on work it takes to keep fleets running.

They’re now applying their experience to the $600B US maintenance market. The average vehicle is getting older and needs more maintenance, but shops struggle to recruit new technicians to replace experienced workers as they retire. This leaves shops turning away work and customers waiting longer for service.

Rodeo builds robots that inspect vehicles, diagnose problems, and perform services, starting with routine maintenance like oil and tire changes. Their robots use AI models specialized for multi-step vehicle maintenance tasks and operate autonomously for 96% of execution time on their initial tasks.

articles.name: Saccade
articles.long_description:
Alzheimer's testing today is bottlenecked around the onset of symptoms, when the damage is already done. Current treatments, including the FDA-approved drugs released in 2024, don't reverse the disease; they only slow it down. Earlier detection means earlier intervention.

Eye movement changes linked to Alzheimer's surface sooner than any other biomarker, up to 15 years before symptoms appear.

We deliver a 15-minute VR assessment delivered to patients in longevity clinics:
• Tasks: patients perform visual tasks designed by neurologists to trigger a distinct oculomotor response in people with Alzheimer's or on its path
• Hardware: our patent-pending attachment connects to any VR headset on the market and captures these eye movement patterns.
• Analysis: the patterns are compared against our ML model to produce a risk analysis.

Once classified, patients can access new interventions, such as the FDA-approved drugs. They're also referred to longevity practices, neurology practices or both, depending on their stage of decline.

Testing for the earliest biomarkers allows the earliest possible intervention. In some cases, that slows the disease enough that patients outlive the onset of symptoms and never face memory loss in their lifetime.
articles.one_liner: World's Earliest Test for Alzheimer's Biomarkers

articles.name: Hundred
articles.long_description:
Hundred is an automated inspection system for the components that make up devices like phones, smartwatches, and laptops. Hundred helps factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-100µm visual defects before parts reach the assembly line. 

Designs change so fast that traditional machine vision can't keep up, forcing factories to rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss roughly 15% of defects, and a single bad part can turn a finished device into scrap. Hundred is replacing manual inspection with an imaging rig that scans an entire shipping tray of parts at once. 

The Hundred rig blocks ambient light and uses varied controlled lighting configurations to detect defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials. The controlled environment means Hundred only needs to scan a single good part before it can find defects, categorize them, and assess their severity accurately.

Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, a problem Hundred's CEO, Erica, saw firsthand as a mechanical engineer designing devices at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani, Hundred's CPO, at Columbia University's admitted-students day in 2017 and Imani went on to spend five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day. Erica later met Iris, Hundred's CTO, in the Bay Area. Iris worked as a quant at Citadel before pivoting to study at Imperial College London where she researched machine learning on 3D meshes and other structured data. Together, they're building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't still exist in 2026.
articles.one_liner: 100% automated inspection for precision hardware parts

articles.name: Ageospatial
articles.long_description:
Ageospatial helps organizations value the risk on their physical assets (properties, land, infrastructure) remotely using satellite imagery.

97% of commercial properties are never physically inspected because it's too slow and expensive. So insurers price risk based on what the client or broker tells them, and about half the time at least one of those records is wrong. The result is mispricing, fraud, and an estimated $36B in premium leakage every year in the US alone, which gets exposed the moment a disaster hits.

Upload a list of addresses and their GeoAI reads satellite and street-level imagery, maps, real-time data, public records and the insurer's own data to determine what's really there, which natural and human hazards surround it, what changed over time, and which properties are worth inspecting. Each property becomes a living record that underwriting, claims and pricing teams can trace from past to present. Ageospatial deploys inside carriers and MGAs as an AI-native service, so insurers get outcomes delivered.

articles.name: Viraj Aero
articles.long_description:
Viraj Aero builds gas turbines that deliver both power and cooling water for data centers. It needs no grid connection and no water pipeline.

Burning natural gas already produces water. Our patented system captures that water from the exhaust. Part of it cools the data center. The rest is turned into steam and injected back into the turbine. That gives up to 40% more power from the same fuel (cheaper compute) and cuts NOx emissions by up to 99%, which cuts permit approvals from years to weeks.

We're building a genset around our first-of-its-kind gas turbine. It fits in a 10-foot container and runs anywhere, even in the desert. That matters because two-thirds of new data centers are being built in water-stressed regions.

We first built this steam-injected turbine for aircraft, where carrying water tanks isn't an option and efficiency is critical. We're currently integrating our full-scale prototype into an aircraft. The team comes from GE, Rolls-Royce and Formula 1, and we're already working with Safran, one of the world's largest aircraft engine manufacturers.

articles.long_description:

Frontier VLMs that can unlock this (like Gemini) are too expensive to run at the volume real industries have, too generic for any single task, and can't be deployed on-prem where sensitive video lives.

We are building an auto vision factory: take video plus a customer's objective, distill a frontier model, and post-train a small open model that is SOTA on that one task and serve it blazingly fast. Our first product, Marlin, is a 2B-parameter open-weights video VLM that matches Gemini-2.5-flash on dense captioning and temporal grounding at a fraction of the cost.

articles.name: Nxtcure Labs
articles.long_description:
NxtCure Labs is an AI-native, full-stack CRO built to take therapeutics from discovery to market faster. We are reinventing medicine from lab to drug discovery.

About 2 million Americans are diagnosed with cancer every year. Science has never moved faster, new immunotherapies, targeted drugs and cancer vaccines arrive every year. But roughly 90% of cancer drugs fail in clinical trials, and about 80% of trials run late. The breakthroughs exist. The way we test them is stuck in the last century.

NxtCure is building autonomous clinical trials. Before a single patient enrolls, we run the trial thousands of times on digital twins. Each virtual patient is a system of coupled differential equations that track how a drug moves through plasma, tumor and heart, and how the tumor grows, shrinks or fights back. The parameters are fit to real trial data, so every twin behaves like real biology. Across thousands of simulations we can calculate the odds that a dose will hit its endpoints, and fix the protocol before it costs anyone time, money or hope.

Then 13 AI agents run the trial. Each one owns a stage: drafting the protocol, ranking sites, pre-screening patients, forecasting drug supply, watching for adverse events, predicting dropout, cleaning data and writing the final report. As real data comes in, the twins update and flag problems weeks before a human would see them.

In 2025, the FDA laid out how computer simulation can take its place. Soon a cancer drug will run through thousands of simulated trials before it ever touches a lab, and reach patients years faster. We’re building that future.

articles.name: Ignition Benefits
articles.long_description: Ignition is an AI-native employee benefits brokerage for companies with under 200 employees. Health insurance is one of the largest line items these companies carry, and employers absorb 15 to 40% rate increases year after year without ever seeing their own numbers. We have rebuilt the sales and back office to be AI-first. This market represents about $500B of market cap, and those businesses have not fundamentally changed in over 50 years. While scaling Plated, I wore every HR hat from doing payroll myself, to managing a PEO, to eventually hiring an employee benefits broker on our way to 1,500 employees. We wasted over $4M on benefits over 5 years, and I'm building Ignition to help companies under 200 employees avoid making my mistakes.

articles.name: Papaya
articles.long_description:
Papaya is the optimization engine for AI agents. Engineers don't have time to continually improve the agents they've shipped — the context bloat, overly chatty subagents, and broken tool calls sit in production traces nobody reads, quietly hurting agent efficiency. With Papaya they connect their agent directly via SDK, get actionable recommendations on how to improve quality, latency, and cost, and the ones they approve are pushed to production as pull requests.

Papaya runs 200+ research-backed analyses across context, prompts, prompt caching, subagents, and tool calls. Every recommendation is ranked by impact and comes with the production runs that produced it — typically a 20%+ quality improvement on the first workflow analysis.

articles.name: Mirrors
articles.long_description:
Mirrors gives developers the infrastructure to control what production AI agents are told, and when.

Today that's scattered across prompts, skills, memory, and tool descriptions. When an agent breaks a rule, most teams can't tell whether it never saw the rule or saw it and ignored it.

See the mistakes your agent keeps making, write an instruction once, and define where it applies. Mirrors delivers it at that step of the run, shows which sessions it reached, and measures whether it helped. It works with every agent framework and any model.

Every team running agents builds this by hand today. We’re building it once, because as agents take on more of a company’s work, what they’re told becomes how the company runs.

articles.name: Frontrunner
articles.long_description:
Frontrunner lets GTM teams describe the work they need done and deploy agents that run it, connected to their existing tools and data. Our customers are building agents for everything from inbound lead routing to signal-based outbound and multi-touch attribution. Think Cursor for GTM: the place to engineer your revenue factory. 

GTM engineers and rev ops teams spend their days stitching tools together; and fielding requests from sales and marketing. Each campaign has its own version of who the customer is, what makes a lead qualified, and which signals matter. When the business changes, someone has to update that logic everywhere. Even teams that can build their own tools end up depending on the person who built them to keep everything running.

Not only does Frontrunner give those agents a shared understanding of your ICP, customers, and gtm motion, but persists that shared understanding automatically when business context changes so that it remains in sync. Sales and marketing build, run, and manage agents against that shared context, using the tools they already know. As prospects move from first touch to closed deal, the results feed back into how agents target, qualify, and engage the next account. Your revenue factory gets smarter with every cycle, optimizing for conversion across the full sales journey.

Our customers range from AI native startups to agencies running GTM for their clients to established businesses supporting large sales teams. They use Frontrunner to turn their best plays into agents their whole team can use.

articles.name: Boat
articles.long_description:
**Problem**

Humans used to need laptops to do their work. Now they prompt agents instead, and those agents need computers too: always-on, in large quantities, and with unlimited capabilities. 

Building and maintaining that yourself is far from trivial.

**Solution**

Boat provides powerful, simple, permissive Ubuntu VMs in the cloud. In a sandbox, an agent can work for long periods on code or on knowledge work like legal, research, reporting, and auditing.

**Why Boat and not any other cloud VM?**

1. It is ready out of the box: every sandbox ships with a desktop, chrome, languages, docker, snapshots, and templates, plus a CLI, SDK, API, and control pane for your fleet.
2. It is permissive and paradigm agnostic: any number of agents can use any number of sandboxes. Agents can run inside or use sandboxes as an external tool.
3. It is expertly crafted: we manage everything from the individual CPU to the orchestration software, which makes sandboxes stable, persistent, scalable, and secure.
4. It is the best performance and price in town: our CPUs rank first on HPC benchmarks, and sandboxes are typically 9x to 18x cheaper than other leading sandboxes.

**Further notes**

Sandboxes are hosted in Europe, which keeps prices low, and more regions are coming. Unless compliance requires it, agents don't notice the region they run in.
articles.one_liner: The best cloud VMs for billions of agents

articles.name: herdr
articles.long_description:
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them — for hours, sometimes days — across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed.

Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue — working, blocked, done, across every project — so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops.

Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.

articles.name: Definite
articles.long_description:
Definite connects operational data with finance so businesses that make, move, build or operate things can see what each production run, load and job actually cost.

These businesses already record a lot: production runs, shipments, job sites, equipment hours, work orders. Finance records the same business in a different shape. Operating systems track activity by site, line, or day. The ledger tracks it by entity, account, and month. Both sets of records exist, but the link between an operating decision and its financial effect usually lives in spreadsheets and in a few people's heads.

So questions that should be routine take days. What happens to cash if one plant adds a shift? How does a change in throughput or staffing flow into the forecast? Which operating changes actually moved the numbers last quarter?

Definite connects to existing operational and financial systems read-only. Models propose how operational records map to financial ones and explain what they find. Deterministic rules perform the calculations and checks, so results trace back to the source records they came from. 

Definite started in a plant office an hour from campus, watching a controller rebuild the same spreadsheet she rebuilds every month to tie her production system to her ledger. The three of us met at the University of Waterloo and had each spent our careers on a version of that join. Gurshabd built wallet policy and approval controls at BitGo, where proving customer assets matched the ledger was still done by hand. Farhan built recommendation systems for Instagram Reels at Meta, joining billions of raw events to the numbers the business reported. Mazin built trading systems at Optiver, then agents for financial analysts at Boosted.ai, where analysts would not act on a number they could not trace. In finance that work is at least funded. In companies that make and move things, nobody had built it at all.
articles.one_liner: Connect operational data with finance to see what drives the numbers.

articles.name: Degla Inc
articles.long_description:
Degla AI builds autonomy software that enables drones to understand spoken instructions, reason onboard, and adapt as the mission unfolds. Once you’ve expressed your intent, the system owns the problem.

An operator can say, “Find the missing hiker wearing a red sweater.” The drone plans the mission, interprets what it sees, and adjusts its flight as new information emerges. The operator sets the objective and the aircraft handles the execution.

At the core is an onboard vision-language model that interprets what the drone sees, understands the operator’s intent, and guides mission planning, execution, and adaptation. Running locally on NVIDIA Jetson, it makes mission decisions without relying on cloud inference.

articles.name: Vibe Robotics
articles.long_description:
Vibe Robotics builds robots for the work nobody should have to repeat.

Every day in every hotel, towels go up to rooms, linens move between floors, and stacks of laundry need to be folded before the next guests arrive. It’s hard, physical, and hotels can’t hire enough people to do it.

Vibe 01 is built for exactly that. It carries, delivers and folds. Two arms, a lift column, and a camera head on a base that drives itself through back-of-house hallways and service elevators. It learns by watching people do the job, then does it on its own. Vibe 01 can already fold a towel fully autonomously in 23.8 seconds, a skill it learned from just a few hundred human demonstrations.

We’re Archer, Daniel, Katherine and Pranav. We’re starting in hotels and building toward everywhere people work.
